sources.citation: Gerstner-Link, Claudia. 2023. Multilateral lexical transfer among four Papuan language families: Border, Nimboran, Sentani, and Sko. In M. Klamer & F. Moro (eds.), Traces of Contact in the Lexicon, 263-306. Leiden: Brill (OA). doi:10.1163/9789004529458_009
sources.note: Cites Pagi forms from 'Gerstner-Link 2000. Pagi fieldnotes' (text and Appendix pp. 301-303: ki 'tree', kai 'feather', mɛki 'tongue', wɔk 'dog', nɔpuni 'night', etc.) for segmental correspondences Waris/Kilmeri/Pagi. Kilmeri forms occasionally carry acute = stress, but no Pagi form is stress-marked and nothing is said about Pagi prosody.

sources.citation: Gerstner-Link, Claudia. 2019. Loans into and from Kilmeri as indicators of the people's migration route. Handout, 11th International Austronesian and Papuan Languages and Linguistics Conference (APLL11), Leiden, June 2019. 11 pp. PDF formerly hosted on M. Klamer's VICI project site.
sources.note: Nothing for Pagi. The handout treats Kilmeri migration, Elseng as a Border language, and Kilmeri-Nimboran loans; its only mention of stress (p.8) concerns the transcription of Nimboran words after Anceaux 1965.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. 1975. Sko, Kwomtari, and Left May (Arai) phyla. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 849-858. Canberra: ANU. hdl:1885/252979 [reprinted in Lynch (ed.) 1981, Readings in the Comparative Linguistics of Melanesia]
sources.note: Tone statements concern the Sko phylum only ('The phylum as a whole is characterised phonologically by the presence of some semantic tone and complex consonant clusters.. Krisa and Rawo may have two tones only'; Vanimo 'Tone is phonemic'). Nothing prosodic about Pagi.

sources.citation: Gerstner-Link, Claudia. 2026 [2025]. Clans, spirits, land and food: Kilmeri texts (Open Text Collections 7). Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: pp.148-149 only: Pagi grammatically closer to Waris/Imonda than to Kilmeri, migration hypothesis, E/W split of Pagi territory. Nothing on Pagi phonology or stress.

sources.note: Lexical forms and segmental correspondences only (e.g. 'The word for "tongue" is bɛr in Kilmeri, mɛki in Pagi, mindɛ in Waris', p274); the chapter's stress remarks concern Nimboran and Kilmeri loanwords, its tone remarks Skou/Wutung. No Pagi prosody.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Sec. 2.6.2.2.11.2 'The Border Stock' (pp. 414-417), 2.6.2.2.11.2.3 'The Bewani Family' (p. 417). hdl:1885/252967
sources.note: Nothing for Pagi or any Bewani-family language: the Border Stock section gives phoneme inventories and grammar notes only for Waris, Manem, Awyi and Taikat (Irian side, from Voorhoeve 1971) and for the Bewani Family only location and speaker numbers. The chapter's stress/tone remarks (e.g. 'There are no tones, and stress is phonemic') belong to other stocks.
